correctness.rationale: In the canonical Euclidean embedding Q_n=conv{L_ne_i}, the interior Gram principal block (L_n^2)_{2..n-1} is Toeplitz with bands 6,-4,+1. Positive coefficients w_i=binom(i,2)binom(n-i+1,2)/B, B=binom(n+2,5), sum to one by Vandermonde. The fourth finite difference of quartic F(j)=j(j+1)(m+1-j)(m+2-j) is 24, including boundary rows because F vanishes at j=-1,0,m+1,m+2. Hence K w=(6/B)1, c=Lw, and each interior column lies at distance squared 6-6/B. The two endpoints are at 2+6(n-1)/B, giving clearance 4-6n/B, exactly zero at n=4 and strictly positive for n>=5. The weighted squared-distance identity R^2+||y-c||^2 forces a unique smallest ball for ALL y in the affine hyperplane, not just a vertex circumcircle. The center is the negative second difference of w and equals the displayed quadratic formula; the n=3 positive weights (7,13,7)/27 and R3^2=98/27 were checked separately. Exact independent rational reconstruction of full L columns for 3<=n<=23 passed. No proof of arbitrary trees or of any other Euclidean embedding is asserted.
